Loosely based on the story of Stephen Glass, who ignited a scandal when his made-up journalism for The New Republic was exposed, the show receiving its world premiere at MCC Theater feels both overly familiar and superficial.
“The Connector” is pitch perfect regarding a magazine’s office politics, and it’s way off key on the much bigger picture of fake news.
The Connector is a tedious shuffle to Ethan’s inevitable unmasking.

The Connector provides much to consider.

The world premiere musical “The Connector” with a book by Jonathon Marc Sherman and music and lyrics by Jason Robert Brown now playing at MCC Theater certainly has a suitable title on many different levels.

Jason Robert Brown's new musical The Connector boasts one of his very best scores, but Jonathan Marc Sherman's fact-based book regurgitates decades-old scandals about journalists like Stephen Glass and Jayson Blair in a way that muddles his message.
Once we see that Dobson is a fraud – and we see it early on – the story has nowhere to go.
A story that should be tense and propulsive feels strangely flat, and its intellectual ambitions still in progress.

cn.t: Brown's score earns widespread praise, but critics find Sherman's book about journalistic fabrication feels dated and muddled. Strong vocal performances, particularly from Ross and Cruz, can't fully overcome structural issues in this timely yet uneven musical.

vr.q: In the end, I thought it was a cool piece but it's not screaming Broadway to me just yet.
